# Core predicates

<!-- Generated by `uv run python -m epistrel.tools.predicates --write` from
     `src/epistrel/core/propositions/vocabulary.py`; CI checks it with `--check`. -->

The predicates Epistrel ships (FR-PROP-5), with the semantics the contradiction rules
read (FR-PROP-3, FR-PROP-10). Each has a fixed id. Arguments are entity kinds, literal
kinds or `any`; the uniqueness key is the subject plus the key qualifiers, and
qualifiers outside the key never take part in uniqueness. A symmetric predicate is
stored with the lower entity id first, and an inverse as its twin (FR-PROP-3).

Three layers give predicates their semantics (FR-PROP-4): this core vocabulary, the
predicates a scenario's author declares (`starting_state.predicates`, with
`closed_sets` and implication `rules`), and **auto-registration**: a relation a
render uses that nobody declared is registered with the weakest semantics — `multi`,
no maximum, no exclusions, implications or containment — so it is remembered but never
contradicted on semantics it was not given (only a direct affirmed-versus-negated
conflict). The engine may propose strengthening one; nothing changes until the author
approves it (`POST /stories/{id}/predicates/{predicate_id}/approve`).

The core vocabulary ships **no implications** between the education predicates: team
membership does not imply enrollment, enrollment does not imply a degree, and a degree
does not name its only institution. An author declares such rules where they hold.

## Identity

| Predicate | Subject → object | Cardinality | Temporal | Direction | Exclusions, containment | Qualifiers | Projection | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `same_as`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000001` | any → any | multi per (subject) | permanent | symmetric | — | — | — | The two entities are one referent ("the stranger" is Bobby). Identity is an ordinary proposition with a holder, so one character may know it while another does not; merges and splits found later are amendments (FR-PROP-7). |

## Location and presence

| Predicate | Subject → object | Cardinality | Temporal | Direction | Exclusions, containment | Qualifiers | Projection | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `located_at`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000002` | any → place | functional per (subject) | fluent | — | containment by `located_in` | — | placement | Where the subject is: one place at a time. A place that contains the other (through `located_in`) is no conflict: Columbus and Ohio agree. |
| `present_at`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000003` | any → any | multi per (subject) | fluent | — | — | — | scene | The subject takes part in a scene or an occasion; several at once are allowed. |
| `located_in`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000004` | any → any | multi per (subject) | permanent | — | — | — | — | Containment of places and organizations (Columbus `located_in` Ohio): the hierarchy `located_at` and the contradiction rules read. |
| `adjacent_to`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000030` | place → place | multi per (subject) | fluent | symmetric | — | `barrier` (str) | — | The two places adjoin (symmetric), with what stands between them as the optional `barrier`: `none`, `door_open` (the default), `door_closed`, `window`, `thin_wall` or `wall`. Perception routing (#161) reads it: an eavesdrop is plausible through anything but a `wall`, and a sound crosses anything but a `wall`. A later declaration of the pair ("she closes the door") is the barrier from then on. |

## Possession

| Predicate | Subject → object | Cardinality | Temporal | Direction | Exclusions, containment | Qualifiers | Projection | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `holds`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000005` | any → item | multi per (subject) | fluent | — | — | `quantity` (str) | placement | The subject physically has the item; a person may hold several. Its inverse `held_by` is functional: an item is in one pair of hands at a time. An optional `quantity` (`<number> <unit>`, "40 silver") says how much of it (#148's detectors). |
| `held_by`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000006` | item → any | functional per (subject) | fluent | inverse of `holds` | — | — | — | The inverse of `holds`, stored as `holds`: an item has one holder at a time. |
| `owns`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000007` | any → any | multi per (subject) | fluent | — | — | — | — | Ownership, independent of who holds the thing now. |
| `consumed`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000027` | any → item | multi per (subject) | event | — | — | `quantity` (str) | — | The subject used up the item (ate, drank, burned, spent it) at the instant: an event, with an optional `quantity`. Claim detection (#148) writes it for consumption language. |

## Life and death

| Predicate | Subject → object | Cardinality | Temporal | Direction | Exclusions, containment | Qualifiers | Projection | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alive`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000008` | person → none | functional per (subject) | fluent | — | excludes `dead` | — | — | The subject is alive (no object); negated, not alive. Excludes `dead` over overlapping time. |
| `dead`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000009` | person → none | functional per (subject) | permanent | — | excludes `alive` | — | — | The subject has died (no object): from then on, permanently. Excludes `alive` over overlapping time and so closes its interval. |
| `born`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000010` | person → none | functional per (subject) | event | — | — | — | — | The subject's birth (no object): a unique event per person, so two different birth times contradict, while a coarser time compatible with canon does not. |
| `injured`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000028` | any → none | multi per (subject) | event | — | — | `cause` (id) | — | The subject was hurt at the instant (no object): an event, with the entity that caused it as the optional `cause`. Claim detection (#148) writes it for injury language. |

## Perception and communication

| Predicate | Subject → object | Cardinality | Temporal | Direction | Exclusions, containment | Qualifiers | Projection | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `on_channel`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000031` | person → str | multi per (subject) | fluent | — | — | — | — | The subject is on a remote channel (a call in progress, a radio link), named by a free-text token (a `str` literal, no entity). Perception routing (#161) lets a `remote_channel` qualifier reach exactly the channel's participants, wherever they are. |
| `spoke_to`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000032` | person → person | multi per (subject) | event | — | — | — | — | The subject said something to the object at the instant: the observable envelope of an utterance (FR-TURN-2), which a character perceives without its words. |
| `spoke`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000033` | person → none | multi per (subject) | event | — | — | — | — | The subject said something (no object, no addressee) at the instant: the envelope of an utterance addressed to no one in particular. |

## Tracked values

| Predicate | Subject → object | Cardinality | Temporal | Direction | Exclusions, containment | Qualifiers | Projection | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `state_value`<br>`01JPRED0000000000000000035` | any → any | functional per (subject, state) | fluent | — | — | `state` (id, key) | — | A story State's value (#191, FR-STATE-8, FR-VERIFY-7): the `state` qualifier is the State's id, the subject the character a per-character State belongs to (the State's own id for a story State), the object the value as a literal. Its canon is the State's fold at the claim's position (`core.states.verify`, an owner lookup), never a fact: an objective or narrator claim is `supported` when the fold equals it (a number within the State's tolerance) and `contradicted` otherwise. A character's belief about a value is an ordinary belief, acquired by observation or testimony. |
